name: Dotted Line Face
baseMeaning: A face made of dotted lines, appearing faded or invisible.
tldr: 🫥 means the sender is fading out, becoming invisible, or leaving without a proper goodbye.

contextMeanings.meaning: 🫥 signals that the sender is deliberately disappearing from their previous life or current presence.
contextMeanings.example: new city, new me, old me 🫥

contextMeanings.meaning: In dating chats, 🫥 can announce that the sender is no longer genuinely interested or available.
contextMeanings.example: i'm not really into this anymore 🫥

contextMeanings.meaning: As a bare or nearly bare reply, 🫥 can express the sender's decision to stop participating in the conversation.
In a work thread, 🫥 can mark the sender's withdrawal from a discussion or project, though the ambiguity can cause trouble.
contextMeanings.example: i'm stepping away from this project now 🫥

platformNotes.note: On Instagram, putting 🫥 alone in a bio or beside a place suggests that the person has erased an old version of themselves. In direct messages, it can close a conversation without a conventional goodbye.

On TikTok, 🫥 can work as a comment announcing that the poster has left the topic or stepped away from the conversation. Younger users are more likely to understand its deliberate disappearance meaning.
In Slack, a lone 🫥 may look like a comment on whether the sender is still taking part in the channel. Because workplace messages need clearer handoffs, naming the change is usually less confusing.
On Discord, 🫥 can punctuate a server exchange about muting, leaving, or fading from a community. In a casual chat it may simply mirror another user's own disappearance joke.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z is the group most likely to use 🫥 as an explicit self-erasure emoji. Its dotted outline closely matches the language of quietly leaving without explaining.
Millennials may recognize 🫥, but younger users have adopted it more readily because it arrived in Unicode 14.0. It can still read as an intentional goodbye rather than a literal disappearance.
Older users are less likely to use 🫥 because the emoji has not spread as widely among them. They may need the surrounding message to understand that the sender is withdrawing on purpose.

warnings.title: Missed as an intentional exit
warnings.description: Someone unfamiliar with 🫥 may treat the dotted face as a rendering problem or miss the self-erasure message. In an important conversation, say plainly that you are leaving, disengaging, or changing your status.

warnings.title: Too vague at work
warnings.description: A lone 🫥 in a work channel can be mistaken for inactivity or a reaction to someone else's message. State what you are ending or who should take over instead of leaving only the emoji.

seoDescription: What does 🫥 mean? It says the sender has faded out, become invisible, or is leaving a conversation without a formal goodbye.

longForm.overview:
The moment 🫥 appears as a bare reaction, the sender is announcing that they have already begun to disappear. Younger users are more likely to send it because it turns quiet withdrawal into an explicit signal: the message says, “I am not fully here anymore.” Used alone in a thread, it can mean the sender has stopped participating; used in a bio, it can suggest that someone has erased the life or identity attached to that account.

🫥 is more deliberate than the 👋 wave and more final than the 🙃 reaction that pretends a fading conversation is merely casual. It also differs from 👻, which still tends to appear in Halloween posts, playful “boo” messages, and flirt about haunting someone’s messages. The melting face 🫠 says “I am dissolving” with greater emotional strain, while 🫥 presents a cleaner outline: the person has become invisible on purpose.

That distinction matters because the dotted face can look like an ordinary fading or image error until the recipient knows the newer meaning. In the right circle, it is unusually honest about withdrawal. Elsewhere, it can seem cryptic, careless, or simply broken.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🫥 first tends to appear when a conversation has already run its course and the sender wants to leave without writing a formal goodbye. As the only reply, it says, “I am not really here” or “I have stopped engaging.” In a bio, especially by itself or beside a city, it can announce that the sender has vanished from an earlier chapter of life. A post such as “new chapter 🫥” treats the emoji as the final mark of a dissolved identity.

The same bare reaction can be playful among friends who already understand the disappearing act. There, sending 🫥 after an exaggerated goodbye continues the joke and avoids an uncomfortable direct farewell. In less familiar settings, the sender may still expect it to communicate that the exit was deliberate.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Avoid 🫥 when the practical consequence of leaving matters more than the atmosphere. Work handoffs, family plans, and dating decisions can suffer when the message is too easy to misread. A recipient who does not know the emoji may see an image glitch, while an older user may simply miss the intended announcement that the sender is withdrawing.

It is also a poor substitute for a necessary boundary. If the point is that you no longer want to continue a conversation, write that you are ending it. If the point is that you have changed jobs, moved away, or want to stop replying to someone, name the change. 🫥 works best among people familiar with its meaning or in a playful conversation where nobody needs further instructions.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone sends 🫥 as a joke, match the exit with 👋 or 🫠 and keep the bit moving. A reply such as “the outline says hi 🫥” acknowledges that you understand they are fading out. If they pair it with “new chapter” or a new city, you can celebrate the change instead of treating the emoji as a final warning.

If it lands seriously, do not reply with another disappearance emoji and leave the uncertainty unresolved. Ask whether they are stepping away for good or simply closing the thread. If 🫥 appeared on your own post, you can answer with a direct “I’m leaving this conversation for now 🫥” to remove any doubt. When the sender appears to be ending a relationship or working arrangement, prioritize a clear statement over matching the visual joke.

faqs.question: What does 🫥 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: It usually means he is fading out, disengaging, or signaling that he is no longer fully present. The sender’s gender does not change the basic meaning, so context matters more than who sent it.

faqs.question: Is 🫥 flirty?
faqs.answer: 🫥 has no inherent romantic meaning. It can appear in a flirtatious exchange as a playful way to describe vanishing, but it more directly announces withdrawal.

faqs.question: What does 🫥 mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: On TikTok, it usually means the sender is leaving the topic, stepping away from the exchange, or presenting themselves as already invisible. Younger TikTok users are especially likely to understand that self-erasure meaning.

faqs.question: What does sending 🫥 in a bio mean?
faqs.answer: It suggests that the person has disappeared from an earlier identity, place, or chapter of life. Beside a city, it can mean they are presenting a move as the erasure of their previous life.

conversationExamples.message: i’m done pretending i’m still coming to those brunches 🫥
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is joking that they have quietly dropped out of a recurring social plan. Respond with teasing recognition, such as “so you’re officially an outline now?”

conversationExamples.message: i don’t think i’m actually interested in taking this further 🫥
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is a softened version of ending the dating connection. A direct reply should confirm whether they want to stop rather than merely joking about disappearing.

conversationExamples.message: i’m stepping away from this project after the handoff 🫥
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is marking a work withdrawal, but the emoji leaves the handoff unclear. Ask who is taking over and what still needs action.

conversationExamples.message: changing my number and letting this old chapter go 🫥
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is using the emoji to describe a deliberate break from their former life. Confirm the practical details with them directly if you need to stay in touch.
A lone 🫥 says the sender is no longer fully engaged and may be exiting the thread. Reply with “you fading out for real?” if the exact intent matters.
